adria.title: Adria
adria.note: The sea Paul's ship drifted across in the storm before the wreck, the central Mediterranean between Crete, Sicily and Malta.

agabus.title: Agabus
agabus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
agabus.note: A prophet at Antioch who said a severe famine was coming. It came in the reign of Claudius, and the church sent relief to the believers in Judea.

agrippa.title: Agrippa
agrippa.about: Tetrarch living at the time of the New Testament
agrippa.note: Herod Agrippa the Second, the last king of the Herodian line. Paul made his defence before him and his sister Bernice, and Agrippa told him he had almost persuaded him to become a Christian.

ananias-3.title: Ananias
ananias-3.about: High Priest living at the time of the New Testament
ananias-3.note: One of 3 men called Ananias. This one is a high priest from the New Testament, named twice in Acts.

ananias.title: Ananias
ananias.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
ananias.note: He was the disciple in Damascus who restored Paul's sight and baptised him. He was afraid of the man who had been persecuting Christians, and he went anyway.

antipatris.title: Antipatris
antipatris.note: Herod the Great built it on the Roman road between Jerusalem and Caesarea and named it for his father Antipater. Soldiers brought Paul there by night, under guard, after a plot against his life came out. The site is Tel Aphek.

appii.title: Appii
appii.note: Appii Forum, a market town on the Appian Way about 43 miles from Rome. Christians came out that far to meet Paul as he was brought to the capital a prisoner.

aristarchus.title: Aristarchus
aristarchus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
aristarchus.note: A Macedonian who travelled with Paul. He was dragged into the riot at Ephesus, sailed with Paul to Rome, and was imprisoned with him there.

asia.title: Asia
asia.note: Not the continent. The Roman province of Asia, in western Asia Minor, with Ephesus among its churches, and the region the seven churches of Revelation belonged to.

bernice.title: Bernice
bernice.about: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
bernice.note: She was Herod Agrippa the Second's sister, and she sat beside him through Paul's defence before Festus, one of the last hearings before Paul sailed for Rome.

caesar-2.title: Caesar
caesar-2.about: Emperor living at the time of the New Testament
caesar-2.note: In Acts the title stands for the emperor of the day, the authority whose court the appeal in Acts 25 went to.

caesar-3.title: Caesar
caesar-3.about: Emperor living at the time of the New Testament
caesar-3.note: Luke puts names to the title: Augustus, under whom Jesus was born, and Tiberius after him.

caesarea.title: Caesarea
caesarea.note: Herod the Great built it as a Roman port on the Mediterranean coast, and it served as the administrative capital of Roman Judea. Cornelius the centurion lived there. Paul spent two years there in prison.

christ.title: Christ
christ.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
christ.note: A title, not a surname. It is the Greek for the Hebrew Messiah, the anointed one, and the New Testament gives it to Jesus of Nazareth as the king, priest and deliverer the Old Testament promised. His life and ministry are under Jesus.

christian.title: Christian
christian.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
christian.note: Outsiders at Antioch coined the word, possibly as mockery, for people who followed Christ. The believers called each other brethren, disciples and saints. It turns up only three times in the New Testament, the last in 1 Peter 4:16, which tells them not to be ashamed of suffering under that name.

cilicia.title: Cilicia
cilicia.note: Paul was born in Tarsus, Cilicia's chief city, on the southeastern coast of Asia Minor. Cilician Jews had their own synagogue in Jerusalem and argued with Stephen there. The province was known for the goat's hair cloth used in tentmaking, which was Paul's trade.

clauda.title: Clauda
clauda.note: Paul's ship got into the lee of this little island off Crete in the storm, long enough to haul in the boat and lash ropes round the hull. It is modern Gavdos, the southernmost point of Europe.

cnidus.title: Cnidus
cnidus.note: Paul's ship struggled to get past this harbour city at the tip of the Cnidian peninsula, in Caria, with the wind against it, and then ran for Crete. Its temple of Aphrodite was famous, and the theatre and harbour works have been excavated.

cos.title: Cos
cos.note: A small island near Rhodes that Paul's ship passed heading back toward Jerusalem. In the first century it was a centre of Hellenistic culture and medicine, with a Jewish community of its own.

crete.title: Crete
crete.note: Paul left Titus here to organise the churches and appoint elders. His ship also put in at the island on the storm voyage to Rome.

cyprus.title: Cyprus
cyprus.note: The island Barnabas came from, where the first missionary journey started and the proconsul Sergius Paulus became an early convert.

damascus.title: Damascus
damascus.note: A city has stood here, on a fertile plain watered by the Barada northwest of Mount Hermon, since before the patriarchs. It was the Aramean capital that fought Israel through the ninth and eighth centuries BC. Saul was converted on the road into it, and the street called Straight was a real colonnaded street whose columns have been found.

drusilla.title: Drusilla
drusilla.about: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
drusilla.note: The youngest daughter of Herod Agrippa I. Felix, governor of Judea, talked her into leaving her first husband, the king of Emesa, and she was sitting beside Felix when Paul spoke about righteousness, self-control and judgment to come. Josephus says she died in the eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79, which some historians doubt.

egyptian.title: Egyptian
egyptian.note: In Acts a Roman officer takes Paul for the Egyptian, a rebel who had recently led an armed rising. Josephus mentions the same man.

euroklydon.title: Euroklydon
euroklydon.note: The wind that drove Paul's ship off course near Crete. Many manuscripts read Eurakylon instead.

felix.title: Felix
felix.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
felix.note: Paul sat in custody at his court for two years. Antonius Felix was the Roman governor of Judea before Festus. He seems to have hoped Paul would pay a bribe, then left him locked up to keep the Jewish leaders happy.

festus.title: Festus
festus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
festus.note: He took over Judea from Felix and inherited Paul as a prisoner. At the hearing Paul used his right as a Roman citizen and appealed to Caesar, so Porcius Festus sent him to Rome.

gamaliel-2.title: Gamaliel
gamaliel-2.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
gamaliel-2.note: Acts names him twice, and he is a man from the New Testament.

gentile.title: Gentile
gentile.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
gentile.note: Anyone who is not Jewish. The Greek word behind it means nation or people, and Paul's gospel turns on Gentiles being grafted into God's covenant people without first becoming Jews, the position defended at the Jerusalem council in Acts 15.

greek.title: Greek
greek.note: Here it means the language, not the people. It is one of the three on the sign Pilate had nailed above Jesus.

hebrew.title: Hebrew
hebrew.note: In the New Testament it means the people, the language, or the way of life. Paul calls himself a Hebrew of Hebrews to say he is all three.

herod-2.title: Herod
herod-2.note: King when Jesus was born. When the magi did not come back to him, Herod the Great ordered the boys of Bethlehem killed. He also enlarged the Jerusalem temple, and Josephus tells his story at length.

isaiah.title: Isaiah
isaiah.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
isaiah.note: Amoz's son, a prophet in Jerusalem in the eighth century, who counselled four kings of Judah and is quoted in the New Testament more than any other prophet. He gave his two sons names that were sermons, Shear-jashub and Maher-shalal-hash-baz. When Sennacherib besieged Jerusalem he told Hezekiah the city would stand, and the Taylor Prism brags of the siege without ever claiming the city fell.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

israelite.title: Israelite
israelite.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israelite.note: One of the people descended from Jacob, who was renamed Israel. Paul calls himself an Israelite in Romans 11 when he argues God has not dropped his people.

italy.title: Italy
italy.note: Aquila and Priscilla had just come from Italy when Paul met them, after Claudius threw the Jews out of Rome. Paul later went there as a prisoner, by way of a shipwreck. Hebrews ends with greetings from "those from Italy".

james-2.title: James
james-2.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
james-2.note: The brother of Jesus. He did not believe during the ministry, then led the Jerusalem church after the resurrection, and the letter of James is traditionally his.

jerusalem.title: Jerusalem
jerusalem.note: David took it from the Jebusites and made it his capital, and once Solomon's temple stood there it was the centre of Israel's worship for a thousand years. Babylon destroyed it, the exiles rebuilt it, Rome destroyed it again in AD 70. Jesus died and rose just outside its walls, and Revelation ends with a new Jerusalem coming down from heaven.

jesus.title: Jesus
jesus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
jesus.note: Born in Bethlehem to Mary and raised in Nazareth in Galilee. Around thirty he began teaching in parables, healing, and gathering twelve disciples, until he was arrested in Jerusalem at Passover, tried before the council and Pontius Pilate, and crucified. His followers said he rose bodily three days later, and the New Testament names him the Messiah, God's own Son become human.

judaea.title: Judaea
judaea.note: The Roman name for the southern part of the land around Jerusalem, roughly old Judah. Client kings of Herod's family ruled it, then Roman procurators like Pontius Pilate. John the Baptist preached in its wilderness and the Passion happened there. After the revolt of AD 66 to 70 Rome struck coins reading "Judaea Capta."

julius.title: Julius
julius.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
julius.note: The Roman centurion of the Augustan Cohort who took Paul and other prisoners to Rome. He was kind to Paul all the way, let him see friends at Sidon, and after the wreck at Malta stopped the soldiers from killing the prisoners.

lasea.title: Lasea
lasea.note: On Crete's south coast, near the harbour called Fair Havens where Paul's ship took shelter. Its ruins were found again in the nineteenth century a few miles east of Fair Havens, just where Luke's account puts it.

lycia.title: Lycia
lycia.note: Mountains and coast in southwest Asia Minor, across from Rhodes. Paul's ships put in at its ports, Patara and Myra.

lysias.title: Lysias
lysias.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
lysias.note: Claudius Lysias, the Roman tribune over the garrison at the Antonia Fortress. He pulled Paul out of a mob in the temple and then sent him under armed guard to Felix in Caesarea with a letter about the case.

lysias-2.title: Lysias
lysias-2.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
lysias-2.note: Acts names him once, and he is a man from the New Testament.

melita.title: Melita
melita.note: Malta. Paul's ship ran aground there in the storm of Acts 27, and he and the others stayed three months before sailing on to Rome. Phoenicians settled it long before, then Carthage and Rome held it, and Punic inscriptions survive from that time.

mnason.title: Mnason
mnason.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
mnason.note: From Cyprus, and a disciple from the earliest days of the Jerusalem church. Paul and his companions lodged at his house in Jerusalem at the end of the third journey.

moses.title: Moses
moses.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
moses.note: Born a Hebrew slave in Egypt and raised in Pharaoh's house, he killed an Egyptian overseer and ran to Midian, where he kept sheep for forty years. God called him back from the burning bush to face Pharaoh and lead Israel out. He gave them the law at Sinai, led them forty years in the wilderness, and died at a hundred and twenty within sight of the promised land.

myra.title: Myra
myra.note: On the coast of Lycia in southwestern Asia Minor. Here the centurion moved Paul and the other prisoners onto a grain ship from Alexandria bound for Italy, the ship that later broke up off Malta. A Roman theatre and rock-cut tombs above the old harbour still stand.

nazarene.title: Nazarene
nazarene.note: It means from Nazareth, Jesus' home town, and it became the name for his followers too, "the sect of the Nazarenes" in Acts 24:5. Matthew ties it to prophecy, possibly playing on the Hebrew word for "branch" in Isaiah 11. Arabic and Hebrew still call Christians by it.

pamphylia.title: Pamphylia
pamphylia.note: Jews from Pamphylia were in Jerusalem at Pentecost. The province lay on the south coast of Asia Minor between Lycia and Cilicia. Paul and Barnabas came ashore at its capital, Perga.

patara.title: Patara
patara.note: It was a port on the Lycian coast of southwestern Asia Minor. Paul changed ships there on the way home from his third journey, taking a larger one across open water to Phoenicia.

paul.title: Paul
paul.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
paul.note: Born Saul, a Jew of the tribe of Benjamin and a Roman citizen from Tarsus. He trained as a Pharisee under Gamaliel and hunted the early church. Then the risen Christ met him in a blinding vision.

paul-2.title: Paul
paul-2.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
paul-2.note: A man from the New Testament. Acts names him 5 times.

pharisee.title: Pharisee
pharisee.about: Religious group in the New Testament
pharisee.note: A Jewish movement devoted to strict keeping of the law, the written text and a large body of oral tradition around it. They carried real weight in the religious life of the people. They argue with Jesus again and again.

phenice.title: Phenice
phenice.note: The King James spelling of Phoenicia, the narrow coast north of Israel where Tyre and Sidon traded. Believers scattered after Stephen's death took the gospel there.

phenice-2.title: Phenice
phenice-2.note: Paul's ship was trying to reach this harbour on the south coast of Crete to spend the winter, and the storm drove it off toward Malta instead. More properly Phoenix.

philip-2.title: Philip
philip-2.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
philip-2.note: Not the apostle. This Philip was one of the seven chosen to oversee the food in the Jerusalem church. He became a traveling evangelist and led the Ethiopian eunuch to faith.

porcius.title: Porcius
porcius.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
porcius.note: Festus's family name. Porcius Festus took over from Felix as governor of Judea, and Paul made his defence in front of him.

ptolemais.title: Ptolemais
ptolemais.note: Paul stopped here and greeted the believers on his way to Jerusalem. It is the old port of Acco under the Greek name it got after the Ptolemaic kings of Egypt took the Syrian coast.

publius.title: Publius
publius.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
publius.note: Paul's ship wrecked on Malta, and Publius, the island's leading official, took them in for three days. Paul healed his father of fever and dysentery. Then the other sick people on the island came.

puteoli.title: Puteoli
puteoli.note: A big Roman port on the Bay of Naples, modern Pozzuoli. Paul landed here after the shipwreck and found believers already in the town. Rome's grain ships came in here.

rhegium.title: Rhegium
rhegium.note: Modern Reggio Calabria, at the southern tip of Italy on the Strait of Messina, and Paul's ship put in briefly on the last leg to Rome.

rhodes.title: Rhodes
rhodes.note: A large island off the southwest coast of Asia Minor, and Paul's ship stopped there. In the ancient world it was famous for the Colossus of Rhodes, one of the Seven Wonders.

rome.title: Rome
rome.note: Capital of the empire that ruled Judea through the whole New Testament period. Paul wrote to the church there, and Acts ends with him in the city as a prisoner, his case appealed to Caesar.

sadducee.title: Sadducee
sadducee.about: Religious group in the New Testament
sadducee.note: A party drawn mostly from the priestly aristocracy. They rejected the oral tradition the Pharisees kept, and they denied the resurrection of the body.

salmone.title: Salmone
salmone.note: Paul's ship, fighting the wind, rounded this cape at the eastern tip of Crete on the way to Rome. It is generally identified with Cape Sidero.

satan.title: Satan
satan.about: An angel in the Old Testament
satan.note: The name means adversary. In Job he questions whether Job's goodness is real, and in Zechariah he stands to accuse Joshua the high priest before the angel of the Lord.

sidon.title: Sidon
sidon.note: The older of the two great Phoenician ports, north of Tyre. It was allotted to Asher, but Asher never took it.

stephen.title: Stephen
stephen.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
stephen.note: He was picked as one of seven to oversee the food for the Greek-speaking widows in the Jerusalem church. He soon became known for miracles and bold debate instead.

syracuse.title: Syracuse
syracuse.note: A Greek city on the southeast coast of Sicily, founded by Corinth in the eighth century BC and once home to Archimedes. Paul's ship stayed three days there on the way to Rome.

syria.title: Syria
syria.note: The region northeast of Israel, called Aram in the Old Testament. In the New Testament Antioch was its chief city and the base Paul's journeys started from, and Luke dates Jesus's birth by a census under Quirinius.

tarsus.title: Tarsus
tarsus.note: Paul was born here, in the capital of Cilicia on the Cydnus River, about twelve miles from the sea, and he called it no mean city. It had schools of philosophy and rhetoric that rivalled Athens and Alexandria.

tertullus.title: Tertullus
tertullus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
tertullus.note: A hired speaker who put the case against Paul before Felix at Caesarea. He flattered the governor for a long time first, then called Paul a troublemaker, a leader of the sect of the Nazarenes, and a man who tried to profane the temple.

trophimus.title: Trophimus
trophimus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
trophimus.note: A Gentile from Ephesus who traveled with Paul. People in Jerusalem thought Paul had taken him into the temple, and that started the riot that ended with Paul under arrest.

tyre.title: Tyre
tyre.note: The leading Phoenician port, partly on the mainland and partly on an island offshore, rich from sea trade and purple dye made from murex shells. Its king Hiram sent cedar and craftsmen for David and Solomon. The prophets attacked its pride and said it would fall.
